page.text:
Addition and multiplication are canonical applications of recursion.
Fixing $m$, addition is the unique function satisfying $0+m=m$ and
$(n+1)+m=(n+m)+1$; multiplication is the unique function satisfying
$0\cdot m=0$ and $(n+1)\cdot m=n\cdot m+m$. Algebraic laws such as
associativity and distributivity are theorems proved by induction, not
clauses silently included in these recursive definitions.
